newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Zhongkang plans IPO of 150 mln A shares.
newsitem.headline: China's Zhongkang plans IPO of 150 mln A shares.

text.p: Television parts maker Shenzhen SEG Zhongkang Co Ltd is planning an initial public offering of 150 million A shares in Shenzhen in 1997, a company spokesman said on Friday.

The company plans to use the funds to expand its production capacity of the glass component of colour television tubes to six million units from the present four million, the official told China Securities Bulletin, a Hong Kong-based newsletter.
It will submit an application for the offering to the China Securities Regulatory Commission in April, he said.
The firm will use the remaining proceeds to make computer screens and whole television tubes, he said.
An underwriter has yet to be selected for the issue and the pricing has not yet been set, the official said.
Zhongkang's total share capital will not be announced until it has restructured its assets, he said. He gave no further details.
State-owned Shenzhen SEG Group, which holds a majority stake in Shenzhen SEG Co Ltd -- China's biggest 21-inch colour television tube maker -- would be one of Zhongkang's major shareholders.

Zhongkang estimated net profits of 170.36 million yuan for 1996, compared with 189.89 million yuan booked for 1995, the official said, adding the drop in earnings was mainly caused by slightly lower sale prices last year.
